subject: Reservation capacity runbook & GPU recommendations - StorCloud RFP
messages:
From: Amanda Lin <amanda.lin@storcloud.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: patrick.oneill@storcloud.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: StorCloud RFP - Dedicated reservation worksheet request

Alex —

Thanks for taking our RFP. To move the procurement review forward we need a detailed capacity worksheet and a recommended GPU mix for our planned workloads. A few context points:

- Primary model: finetuned LlamaX-13B (int8 safe quant) for chat and document summarization.
- Target latency: p95 <= 220ms for 512 token responses (chat interactive).
- Baseline throughput: 120 QPS sustained during business hours (US-EAST) with 2x traffic spikes to 300 QPS for short bursts.
- Average request size: 250 tokens in, 400 tokens out (rough distribution).
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~650 (concurrent KV+chat contexts).
- Required SLA: 99.9% availability for dedicated fleet during business hours; alternative fallback to hosted API acceptable for non-critical routes.

Please include: recommended GPU types and counts for a reserved pool, expected tokens/sec per GPU with the recommended batching profile, an autoscaling/burst plan (how many reserved vs burst capacity), and a simple runbook for capacity failover. Also attach a cost/ops estimate we can present to procurement.

RFP ID: SC-RFP-2026-11
Procurement window: Nov 20, 2026 (internal review)

Amanda Lin
VP of Engineering, StorCloud
amanda.lin@storcloud.com

Attachments mentioned in RFP: baseline_traffic.csv, compliance_summary.pdf

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lin <amanda.lin@storcloud.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Neill <patrick.oneill@storcloud.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: StorCloud RFP - Dedicated reservation worksheet request

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear brief. Attached is a first-pass capacity runbook and the populated worksheet (storcloud_capacity_worksheet.xlsx). High-level recommendation (summary):

1) Reserved pool (predictable baseline):
   - 6 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (pinned to LlamaX-13B int8 variant)
   - Expected steady-state throughput: ~18k tokens/sec per A100 when using continuous batching with 3-6 request groups and KV prefix caching.
   - Effective QPS capacity (chat average 650 tokens total per request): ~55 QPS per A100 sustained -> 6 A100 ~= 330 QPS sustained.

2) Burst/peak capacity (reserved + burst):
   - 2 x NVIDIA H100 (on-call reserved burst) for peak spikes and re-routes; each H100 modeled to provide ~120 QPS for shorter bursts because of larger frequency and faster matmuls.
   - Policy: autoscale to H100 within 90s when 95th percentile queue depth exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 30s windows.

3) Cost and reservation pattern:
   - Baseline: Reserve 6 A100 80GB (monthly commit) to satisfy 99.9% of business hours traffic.
   - Burst credits: 2 H100 reserved as burst pool, plus 1-2 elastic H100s as spotable capacity depending on procurement appetite.

4) Latency SLOs: with the recommended batching profile, expect p95 ~180-220ms for 512-token responses on A100; H100 reduces p95 by ~15-25% for burst traffic. We include KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes, which reduces token generation by average 12% across the workload.

5) Runbook (short):
   - Trigger: queue depth > threshold OR p95 > 240ms for >2min -> promote burst H100 pool and reduce batching window to prioritize latency.
   - Fallback: if H100 not available, route non-critical routes to hosted API (redwood-hosted.fallback) using policy that keeps PII-sensitive routes on dedicated only.
   - Escalation: If availability <99.7% for >10min, page on-call infra and open a bridge; notify customer success and procurement.

I attached a CSV with per-GPU throughput calibrations (redwood_gpu_prescription.csv) and the full worksheet. The worksheet breaks down request mix, tokens/sec assumptions, batching config, and estimated monthly cost at current list rates.

Next steps: we propose a 60-minute technical sizing workshop to validate assumptions (traffic trace, examples of long conversational sessions). Are you available next week?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: StorCloud RFP - Dedicated reservation worksheet request

Amanda / team —

Following Alex's summary, a few technical clarifications and conservative knobs we usually recommend for enterprise customers running finetuned LlamaX-like models:

- Model variants & memory: if you enable 4-bit quant for cold-starts you can reduce memory footprint and increase effective batch sizes on A100; however, for sticky chat workloads where context windows and KV caches are large, we recommend keeping one fleet of 80GB A100s primarily (fewer OOMs, predictable perf).

- Batching and windowing: target 40-60ms batching windows during baseline; shrink to 10-20ms on burst policy to drive latency down at cost of batching efficiency. The worksheet shows expected token/sec curves at both windows.

- Throughput calibration (conservative):
   * A100 80GB: 14k tokens/sec (safe baseline) -> ~42 QPS at 650 tokens avg
   * H100: 22k tokens/sec -> ~80 QPS at 650 tokens avg (good for peak)

- Reservation plan alternative (cost-sensitive): reserve 4 A100 + 3 x borrowed H100 burst credits (cloud partner marketplace) to cut monthly commit by ~18% while still hitting p95 targets most days. Details and tradeoffs in the worksheet.

- Observability hooks: enable per-route token breakdowns, per-GPU utilization dashboards, and canary coverage for model patches. We also recommend storing 7-day token traces to support tuning before procurement sign-off.

I'll be on the sizing call to validate the trace-driven numbers. Alex — can you share the traffic sample (anonymized) ahead of the workshop?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Amanda / Patrick —

Quick follow-up after Marissa and Alex's notes. A couple of numbers we use when sizing reservation commitments so procurement can see worst-case headroom:

- Safety buffer: +25% headroom above sustained predicted QPS. With Alex's 6 A100 baseline that gives ~412 QPS effective capacity (330 * 1.25) which covers most unexpected load and maintenance windows.
- Warmup/scale time assumptions: plan for 60-90s to spin burst H100s from reserved pool; for elastic cloud-burst we use prefer-spot policy but keep 2 H100s reserved to guarantee fast scale.
- Cold-start mitigation: enable prefix/KV cache with 72h TTL for the most common session starters — reduces cold compute by ~9-12% on long-running conversations.

Procurement-facing summary we recommend sending to StorCloud:
   - Commit: 6 x A100 80GB (monthly reserved) + 2 x H100 reserved for burst + 2x elastic H100 for marketplace burst credits.
   - Expected monthly billed tokens & estimated spend: see worksheet tab 'cost_summary'.

If that aligns, Alex can share a short one-pager procurement deck and I'll join the workshop for the technical calibration. Suggested workshop times: Mon 11/23 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue 11/24 14:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks —
